messages:
alex: kicking off canary for api-client v1.11 at 10% — includes paging header rewrite (accepts: serialized-cursor->cursor-bin). starting monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary=10% · image=api-client:v1.11 · sha=428f2b7 · env=prod-canary

priya: noticing spike on /v2/paging from canary customers, lots of 502s with 'invalid cursor' in logs. stack traces point to header decode failures.

lee: getting same for internal test fleet. curl hits fail when `X-Redwood-Cursor` present.

sam (oncall): putting myself onpager. can you dump a raw header sample? @priya @lee

priya: pasted samples in thread: `X-Redwood-Cursor: eyJ2IjoxLCJvZmZzIjowfQ==` — decoder throws json parse error. Looks like server expects base64 protobuf but client sending base64 json.

ops-bot: incident created · sev=2 · incident_id=INC-1769801 · paging-api errors detected in canary region 

alex: ack. rollback option or flip feature-flag? which is faster?

dana: kill flag `ff:paging-new-cursor-encoding` exists for rollout. flip it to off to stop canary behavior.

sam (oncall): flipping kill flag now. command: `redwood feature flip ff:paging-new-cursor-encoding --env=prod --state=off --actor=@sam --note="hotkill canary"`

deploy-bot: feature flip queued -> executed. ff:paging-new-cursor-encoding = OFF.

priya: errors dropping but not gone for a subset — looks like some requests routed to cached canary nodes.

lee: rolling back canary image to v1.10 for affected pool. `redwood deploy rollback --service api-client --to-image api-client:v1.10 --selector=canary-pool-3`

deploy-bot: rollback started for canary-pool-3 

cs-team: FYI customer impact: ~12 customers saw degraded paging behavior between 14:02-14:18 UTC. largest affected: AtlasRetail (session timeouts), BetaPartner (fetch failures). CS alerted and triaging outbound messages.

sam (oncall): coordinating handoff to evening oncall in 45m — leaving notes in incident doc. current status: kill-flag off, rollback in progress, observed errors trending to baseline.

ops-bot: rollback completed for canary-pool-3 · health checks green · routing restored to stable.

priya: confirmed new errors ~0.6% above baseline for a few minutes, then normal. logs show the remaining failures were from clients that reconnected during the header flip; session cleanup helped.

lee: ran quick sync script to evict canary kv from edge caches: `for node in $(list-canary-nodes); do curl -XPOST $node/evict-cache; done` — cleared residuals.

alex: good. create follow-up: add integration test for cursor header serialization mismatch and a canary rollback playbook.

sam (oncall): raising postmortem -> assign to @alex @priya. include customer impact summary and proposed mitigation (feature gating, stronger contract tests, sticky flow for cache eviction).

dana: suggested short-term patch: publish compatibility shim that accepts both cursor encodings and normalizes server-side. can patch in 1 day.

priya: will draft quickfix PR for shim, and schedule canary rollout behind FF with stricter smoke checks.

cs-team: sending customer notes now — templated message and list of affected orgs attached.

alex: thanks everyone. final status: incident resolved, rollback + kill-flag stopped new errors, edge eviction cleared sticky failures. will follow up in postmortem. :thumbsup:

sam (oncall): handing off to @lee for overnight watch. leaving checklist in incident doc and tagging alert group.

lee: received handoff. will watch paging metrics for next 12h and follow up if any regression.

ops-bot: incident INC-1769801 → status=resolved (monitoring) · duration=0h16m53s
